## Small windows

- The sessions pane floats over the tabs when the window is narrow, so terminals keep their full width and don't resize when you open it. Open it from the rail or with Ctrl+Shift+B. Click outside it, press Esc, or open a session to close it. It docks again when the window is wide, with its size and open state unchanged.
- Choose how the sessions pane behaves in Settings > General > Sessions pane: Automatic (float on narrow windows), Float over tabs, or Dock beside tabs.
- On narrow windows the New SSH session button shows only its icon, and quick connect becomes a search button that expands over the menus. Ctrl+Shift+K still opens it.
- A docked sessions pane gets narrower on small windows so the tabs stay usable. Its saved width comes back when the window is wider.
- The window has a minimum size, so the title bar and tabs no longer overlap or get cut off.

## Settings and Welcome tabs

- Drag the Settings and Welcome tabs like any other tab: reorder them, split them into their own pane, or move them to another window.
- On narrow windows or in a split, the Settings sections become an icon rail, then a row across the top.

## Fixes and polish

- The command history result is now shown as a status badge.
- Clicking the selected rail icon now opens the sessions pane when it is closed.

Choose the x64 download for Intel or AMD PCs. Choose ARM64 only for Windows on ARM devices.
